NASA JPL identifies Sagittarius A* as the Milky Way's central supermassive black hole, with about four million solar masses and a distance over 26,000 light-years. It explains that black holes are detected through nearby matter, and that EHT combines radio-wave-capable telescopes worldwide into an Earth-size virtual telescope to image matter surrounding Sagittarius A* and reveal its silhouette.
